prompt: A regional airport seen through its perimeter fence: a chain-link fence with wire in the foreground, a stretch of apron with a parked regional jet and a fuel truck, a low terminal building and a control tower behind, flat prairie and the distant Front Range. Light: late afternoon in autumn, low sun from the side, long shadows, a pale clear sky. A documentary photograph taken by a working photographer in Colorado, not an architectural showcase: eye level, from across the street or the edge of the lot, 35mm lens, ordinary unposed framing. Real-world wear everywhere: weathered concrete, dust, tire marks, dry grass and weeds at the edges, faded paint lines, utility poles and wires, a few ordinary parked cars. Natural, uneven light with no glow, no lens flare, no HDR look, no hyper-clean surfaces, no perfect symmetry. Muted, true-to-life color like an unedited RAW file, fine grain, slightly imperfect exposure. The main subject sits in a horizontal band through the middle of the frame, near the center, so the picture still works cropped to a wide strip or to a tall 4:5 crop. Wide 16:9. No people in uniform and no recognizable people, no readable text, signs, logos, flags, insignia, or watermarks. Not any real, identifiable building. Use the reference photos only for their photographic look: lens, light, color, realism, and the Colorado setting. Do not copy their buildings, mountains' exact shapes, signs, or any text.
